title: Soter Labs can change the subsidy multisig signers unilaterally, bounded only by composition floors
content:
A.6.1.1.4.3.4.2.5 grants the modification power: "Operational GovOps Soter Labs can change the signers of the USDS Demand Subsidies Multisig at any time, so long as there are at least two (2) signers from Soter Labs and one (1) signer from Skybase Foundation, and at least two-thirds of signers are required to execute transactions."

The party holding the signing majority also controls the composition of the signer set, and can exercise that control "at any time" without a proposal, review or vote. The Skybase Foundation's presence is protected only by a floor — it is guaranteed *a* seat, not a specific person, and the floor is stated in Soter Labs' own modification clause.

The three constraints are real but weak in one direction. Requiring ≥2 Soter Labs signers prevents the firm from *dropping below* majority, which protects continuity but not the Agent. Requiring ≥1 Foundation signer keeps the Agent represented. Requiring a ≥2/3 threshold prevents the multisig from being loosened into a single-signature wallet — a genuinely important floor, since it survives any expansion of the signer set.

The tension with the rest of the Artifact is that this is the one place where a non-Agent party can restructure a control mechanism over Skybase's capital without touching the Artifact. Everywhere else, changing who holds authority means editing a `[Core]` document via Root Edit — proposal, Facilitator alignment review, token holder poll. Here the Artifact pre-authorizes the change and records only the invariants.

That may be the right trade for operational key management, where waiting ten days to replace a departed signer is itself a risk. But it means SKYBASE holders' assurance over subsidy capital rests on three numeric floors rather than on any approval right.
description: Modification authority sits with Operational GovOps, subject to keeping at least two Soter Labs signers, at least one Skybase Foundation signer, and a two-thirds execution threshold.
